title: Hydrodynamics without a relaxation gap: memory effects, nonlocality, and superdiffusion
summary: By studying a simple model of relativistic particles propagating through a background medium with an energy-dependent relaxation time that is unbounded from above, we investigate how long-term memory obstructs the emergence of local hydrodynamics in systems with a gapless non-hydrodynamic sector. In the RTA matching frame, we show that the full gradient expansion is generically divergent in most flows, even for Fourier modes, and that any resummation necessarily retains an infinite set of slow non-hydrodynamic degrees of freedom.
